outcome: neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) hospitalization rate
cohort: The study included 1032 pregnant women (128 with recurrent pre-eclampsia with severe features and 904 with initial pre-eclampsia with severe features) who gave birth or terminated pregnancy at 20 weeks of gestation or later at a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2016 and December 2022.
finding: Women with recurrent pre-eclampsia with severe features are more likely to experience adverse perinatal outcomes, including lower gestational age and birth weight, compared to those with initial severe pre-eclampsia.
mod_finding: A history of cesarean section was identified as an independent risk factor for recurrent pre-eclampsia with severe features.
birth_weight: Birth weight was lower in the recurrent PE with severe features group than in the initial PE with severe features group.
gest_age: Gestational age at birth was lower in the recurrent PE with severe features group than in the initial PE with severe features group.
